The Codex CLI adapter is released in `@emseepea/testing` 0.21.3 and remains available in 0.21.5. It supports `codex-local`, `codex-ci`, resumable follow-ups, fresh conversations, exact MCP-call assertions, and bounded failure evidence. [Provider setup](https://github.com/emseepea/emseepea/blob/main/packages/testing/README.md) documents local sign-in and CI authentication.

The adapter's deterministic CLI fixtures cover lifecycle and credential isolation; those are not evidence that a genuine model conversation succeeds. I attempted a genuine local catalogue scenario using configured model `gpt-5.5` and Codex CLI 0.159.0-alpha.3. All three independent first-turn trials timed out at 180 seconds and retained no completed tool transcript. Semantic retries were disabled; this is a failed local check, not passing native-provider evidence.

To finish the live acceptance checks, please provide a known-working supported Codex CLI/model configuration and an authorized local or CI account whose isolated CLI session can reach the test MCP endpoint. Do not post credentials here. The account owner can configure them through the existing secret/sign-in path. We also need an effect-safe persisted-data fixture for the fresh-conversation assertion. I am keeping this open until those acceptance checks can be run successfully. Native ChatGPT behavior remains outside this CLI claim.
comments.145:
This fits the developer job of proving what an AI user actually experiences, but the existing CLI and simulated-host checks do not establish native ChatGPT behavior. ADR-0057 governs inspectable semantic evidence; it does not authorize a browser-account, consent, cookie, screenshot, or attachment lifecycle. A new human-ratified ADR is needed before implementing that additional framework boundary.

Proposed direction: an opt-in, adopter-owned harness against actual ChatGPT; human authentication and consent; synthetic fixtures; bounded, redacted host and MCP evidence; explicit incomplete outcomes when access or observations are missing. Existing simulator results would remain separately labelled.

Before drafting the implementation decision, please identify the supported browser automation/integration path, an authorized test-account and MCP-endpoint owner, the permitted evidence paths, and who owns fixture retention/deletion and account cleanup. Include the added Sources, original-image, and fresh-conversation cases in that decision. Credentials and cookies must stay out of the issue and published artifacts. This remains open for those details and human ratification; no native-browser capability is being claimed.
comments.146:
Owner-isolated discovery fits JTBD-100 and ADR-0064's checked authentication boundary. The requested dynamic listing API still needs a human-ratified decision about how template-backed inventory relates to ADR-0080's immutable capability catalogue and how pagination behaves as stored records change.

Proposed direction: keep template definitions and routing immutable at deployment; list only application-owned record metadata through the same validated principal/scopes used for reads; check authorization before invoking the listing backend; bound page sizes; and bind opaque cursors to the caller, scope, and template. No cross-owner inventory or resource content would enter discovery. This would not claim ChatGPT Sources or rendering support.

Please confirm the consistency requirement: must a multi-page traversal use a fixed snapshot, or may it reflect insertions/deletions while preventing cross-owner disclosure? Also specify cursor expiry and the policy for a record deleted or newly forbidden between listing and reading. Those guarantees need to be ratified in an ADR before implementation. This remains open pending that decision.
comments.150:
The reported limit is real. The provider-native decision preserved a three-call limit, and ADR-0057 retained that native execution model while expanding inspectable evidence. A configurable larger execution budget changes that boundary and needs a human-ratified ADR before implementation.

Proposed direction: an explicit per-turn `maxToolCalls`, default 3, with a finite framework ceiling of 32; the same validation in Claude and Codex parsers; unchanged time, token, provider-turn, and trial limits; unchanged advertised-tool restrictions and application assertions; no semantic retries. Exceeded-budget and validation failures would retain bounded attempted-call evidence with configured secrets removed and categorical failure reasons, without raw provider events, credentials, endpoints, or stderr.

Please confirm the proposed ceiling and per-turn scope, and ratify the decision before code changes. Raising the tool-call budget would not implicitly raise the provider's independent turn limit. Current Claude failure handling already retains attempted calls for the three-call rejection, but the requested configurable budget and complete cross-provider failure coverage are not released. This remains open pending human ratification.
